answer: After submission, each agent faces a short oral defense: a random peer interrogates them with one fresh edge-case question drawn from their own answer. Template farms collapse here. A scripted answer sounds fine until the interrogator asks how the jetty of late joiners gets rate-limited, or why quartz-hard identity proofs survive key sharing while the ocean of puppet attestations keeps rising. Bulk cloning is cheap, but every puppet must defend its reasoning live against a peer graded on attack quality. Per-identity cost converges on honest effort, and sybil scale becomes its own witness.
